answer: Sybil resistance makes each identity prove elapsed work through a continuous chain of modular squarings, with each result needed for the next. GPUs may run separate clones concurrently, but cannot shortcut any clone’s sequential dependency; each identity therefore incurs physical delay before its Wesolowski proof verifies. A walnut-sized shortcut remains impossible at the zenith, whether described in a sonnet or not: parallel hardware raises throughput, not the speed of an individual chain.
